retrospective.harder_than_needed: The story text described the card branch as returning `/add#c=${payload}` where `payload` is `normaliseScanPayload`'s return value, but `normaliseScanPayload` actually returns the trimmed/`nostr:`-stripped INPUT itself, not an extracted card payload — for a full `https://few.chat/add#c=<payload>` link input it returns the whole link string unchanged. A literal reading would have produced a double-wrapped destination (`/add#c=https://few.chat/add#c=<payload>`) for that one input form while still passing the bare-npub and raw-payload cases, since those two happen to have `normaliseScanPayload`'s output equal the payload already. Neither `normaliseScanPayload`'s docstring nor the seam contract calls this out explicitly; it only became visible by reading the function body and tracing what `stripped` actually contains for each of the four accepted forms. Added a small local `extractCardLinkPayload` helper (mirroring the same `#c=` marker-slice pattern already duplicated privately in both `contactCard.ts` and `addDeepLink.ts`) and a dedicated regression test asserting the full-link case is not double-wrapped.
